description: Gate authorization verification (spec 06 section 2). Verify `envelope.authorization` given `requires-gate`, `approvers` and the set of already-seen request hashes. This is the file that makes 'approved is not a boolean' testable.

vectors.name: gated-with-valid-authorization
vectors.description: the approval signature travels inside the envelope and binds this exact action

vectors.name: gated-without-authorization
vectors.description: THE constitutional case: a gated action with no approval signature is rejected. There is no flag, header, binding or ambient marker that can substitute (ADR-0002 anti-lesson)

vectors.name: ungated-without-authorization
vectors.description: no gate rule applies, so no authorization is needed

vectors.name: authorization-for-different-target
vectors.description: a genuine, unexpired, correctly signed approval carried while acting on a different target: re-use across actions is impossible by construction

vectors.name: authorization-for-different-args
vectors.description: same action and target, different arguments: the approval bound args-hash

vectors.name: authorization-for-different-mandate
vectors.description: the approval bound the mandate under which the action was requested

vectors.name: authorization-request-tampered
vectors.description: rewriting the request body breaks the hash the signature covers

vectors.name: decision-signature-invalid
vectors.description: extending the approval window after signing invalidates the signature

vectors.name: approver-not-permitted
vectors.description: a well-formed signature by a human who is not an approver for this scope

vectors.name: self-approval
vectors.description: the requesting subject signing its own approval, even when its key is in the approver set

vectors.name: denied
vectors.description: a signed denial is a record, not an authorization

vectors.name: denied-without-reason
vectors.description: a denial MUST carry a reason: it is the refusal the agent receives and the training data for policy drift learning

vectors.name: approval-expired
vectors.description: the effect was emitted after the approval stopped being usable

vectors.name: used-before-decided
vectors.description: an effect emitted before its approval was signed

vectors.name: request-expired-before-decision
vectors.description: the approver signed a request that had already timed out in the queue

vectors.name: replayed-authorization
vectors.description: single-use: the second effect carrying the same request-hash is rejected

vectors.name: multi-use-authorization-not-replay
vectors.description: single-use false is the only way a second use is permitted, and it is explicit in the signed decision

vectors.name: authorization-present-but-not-required
vectors.description: an authorization that is present is always verified, even when policy did not require one: junk cannot ride along (here the classification no longer matches the approval)
